text:
vivian: Quick recap — kicked off onboarding for vertex-embed-v2 (fp16 -> int8) on the wiki/qa holdout this morning. baseline fp16 recall@1=0.672, int8 per-tensor recall@1=0.597. short log below.

miguel: ouch. can you paste the full recall@k table?

vivian: sure — ran standard suite (wiki/answers/devset).
```
model,recall@1,recall@5,recall@10
vertex-fp16,0.672,0.842,0.901
vertex-int8-pt,0.597,0.800,0.872
vertex-int8-pc,0.645,0.827,0.895
```
pt=per-tensor, pc=per-channel

tara: interesting that per-channel helps a lot. did you use symmetric quant or clamp-based?

vivian: default clamp (max=6) with 8-bit symmetric. used calibration set of 5k samples (same as other onboards).

miguel: also check embedding norms distribution. quant can squash variance and kill nearest neighbor ordering. did you compare L2 norm hist?

vivian: yep — quick diff: mean norm fp16=1.02, int8-pt=0.78, int8-pc=0.96. per-channel keeps norms nearer to fp16.

laura: ran a quick clustering sanity: kmeans k=200 on the eval corpus. silhouette score fp16=0.21, int8-pt=0.12, int8-pc=0.18. so pc still below baseline but much closer.

vivian: repro command I used:
```bash
./eval/embeddings_eval.py \
  --model vertex-embed-v2 \
  --quant int8 --quant-mode per-tensor \
  --calib-file calibs/wiki_5k.npz \
  --holdout datasets/wiki_holdout.jsonl \
  --metrics recall@1,recall@5,recall@10,silhouette,norm_hist
```

miguel: can you try `--quant-mode per-channel --clamp 4.0`? sometimes lower clamp helps with tail stability.

vivian: launching per-channel clamp=4.0 now (job 4321). queue link: https://staging-jobs.redwood/api/jobs/4321

ops-bot: deployment:vertex-embed-v2-int8-pc-clamp4 started on staging (job 4321) — ETA ~12m

tara: another thought — layernorm folding in compilation sometimes changes scale. did you run the no-fold binary?

vivian: not yet. will run a no-fold run after this job.

miguel: also ping eng-runtime for kernel differences; sometimes int8 kernels use different accumulation that slightly shifts dot product ordering.

laura: note for later: add per-example recall breakdown for short vs long queries. we saw short-query recall falloff in earlier onboards.

vivian: good call. enabling breakdown in follow-up job (job 4322).

tara: if per-channel + clamp4 still not acceptable, try mixed-precision fallback for last transformer block (keep fp16 for output projection). we did that on pelican and it saved recall.

vivian: ack — will try mixed-precision if needed. will post results here once jobs finish. :thumbsup:

vivian: preliminary results for job 4321 (int8 pc clamp=4.0): recall@1=0.633, recall@5=0.815, silhouette=0.19. still ~4ppt below fp16 at r@1 but much better than per-tensor.

miguel: that's promising. can we A/B a small canary with fallback to fp16 for high-confidence queries?

laura: we have route-level fallback logic — canary config looks like `canary: {pct:5, fallback_model: vertex-fp16}`. I'll draft a rollout plan.

vivian: thanks — filing a short follow-up ticket for canary plan and mixed-precision experiment. I'll CC eng-runtime and infra.

miguel: awesome. one more nit: document calibration seed and sample selection in the onboarding PR so it's reproducible.

vivian: will do. thanks all.
